description: CASEWORK-B10 C4 (casework.md): loft.cabinets 1.1.0 on P1's +X gypsum face (its left, P1 drawn from the back) in B10 (b10-partitions), the backs at X 182.25, from Y 186 (1/2 in off the back wall's framing) toward the front on the subfloor: V3021 (2 doors under a 6 in false front) at Y 186..156 and VDB1521 (3 drawers, the top front 6, boxes 12.5 x 20 of 1/2 plywood on 1/4 bottoms, 20 in slides) at Y 156..141, 3/4 melamine frameless: 6 036.17578125 in^3, 578.75 in of PVC banding, 4 hinges, 3 slide pairs. 35 bodies. test_casework_b10.py probes it against every solid of b10-partitions. model.json is the plugin's expansion with the member materials documents applies; members.json each body's member metadata (packages/loft-plugins/tests/test_casework_b10.py pins both).
derivation: Every expectation is ANALYTIC, from services/geometry/tests/test_casework_b10.py's independent script (test_casework's script of casework.md's conventions, never the plugin): each panel a box, a notched side its box less its 3 x 4.5 toe notch; summed in exact rational arithmetic (x 25.4 = mm exactly).
surface_area = each panel's box area, a notched side's less twice its notch's face; bodies are separate.
topology: a box 6 faces, 12 edges, 1 shell; a notched side 8 faces, 18 edges. MESH: a box 24 vertices and 12 triangles, a notched side 36 and 20 (two hexagons of 4 triangles, six quads of 2).
tolerance_rationale: Measured first, then set (geometry-gates skill), 2026-10-29: volume 3.1e-7 mm^3 and area 9.3e-9 mm^2 off the exact sums over 35 bodies, centroid 1.8e-12 mm; 1.25e-6 is 4x the worst.
roundtrip_tolerance_rationale: Measured 2026-10-29: the STEP round trip re-sums the 35 solids and moves the VOLUME by 4.5e-7 mm^3; 1.8e-6 is 4x; volume and area only.
